plan: This is an ascending clock auction, and my sealed bid acts as my exit price. To maximize profit, I want to win when the price is below my value and lose when it's above. Bidding my true value is a common strategy in such auctions, as it ensures I never pay more than my value and always win if my value is the highest. Since there's only one round, I'll stick to this straightforward approach.

My goal is to maximize profit. In a sealed-bid ascending clock auction, bidding your true value is often a good strategy to avoid the winner's curse and ensure positive profit if you win. Since I don't know the other bidders' values, and bids are independent each round, I will bid my true value to guarantee a non-negative profit if I win.

My value is $28. In an ascending clock auction, the optimal strategy for a bidder is to bid their true value. This ensures I win if and only if my value is higher than the other bidders' values, and I pay the second-highest bid. Since all values are equally likely between $0 and $49, bidding my value maximizes my expected profit.
